newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar closes weaker on year-end selling.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar closes weaker on year-end selling.

text.p: * Canada's dollar closed weaker at C$1.3666 (US$0.7318) on Monday from Friday's close at C$1.3628 (US$0.7338) in thin trading, dealers said.
* They said the currency softened on year-end selling and was spurred on by weaker Canada and U.S. bond markets. * There was no sign of Bank of Canada intervention.
There was no sign of Bank of Canada intervention despite the currency softening past key support at C$1.3650, dealers said.
"It's probably not the type of weakness that worries the Bank of Canada too much," said Gregory.
Dealers said they expect the currency to continue trading weaker this week in thin volumes heading into the Christmas season. They said C$1.3680 is a key support figure to watch.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar slumped to 1.1297 marks from Friday's close at 1.1403 mark and slid to 83.23 yen from Friday's 83.55 yen.
